title: The Arthur count
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Tuesday. The owner has said 'Arthur' once since he started, and the strip counted. Today she says 'Wood' for the first time, by accident, reading the digest's margin. She corrects herself. He says either. She says Arthur, and it's the second.

panels.composition: The shop. The OWNER at the counter with a digest — one of his, left on the counter. Reading the margin. WOOD at the cutter.

image.prompt: a woman in reading glasses at a shop counter reading the margin of a small photocopied booklet while a young man works at a mat cutter, black and white, no words
a young man at a mat cutter, not turning around, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The owner setting the digest down. The margin. The gull. Her thumb beside it.

image.prompt: close on a small booklet on a counter with a woman's thumb beside the two-stroke mark in its margin, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The shop. The mat cutter going. The strip's count in the corner of the panel, tiny, like the sign's marks: two. Nobody else in the strip keeps count. The strip does.

image.prompt: a small frame shop interior with a young man cutting a mat and a woman at the counter, two tiny tally marks in the panel's corner, black and white, no words
image.notes: The 'Arthur' count per characters.md: Oct 2000 is the third (the fresh blade). This is the second.

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'No. Arthur.' The second. The strip keeps the count in the corner.
